problemStatement.formal: r_3(N) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq [N],\ A \text{ contains no 3-term arithmetic progression}\} = o(N).
problemStatement.plain: Roth's theorem says that any "dense enough" subset of the integers must contain a 3-term arithmetic progression (three equally spaced numbers like 3, 7, 11). No matter how cleverly you try to avoid creating such patterns, if your set occupies a positive fraction of {1, 2, ..., N}, a 3-term AP will appear once N is large enough. This is the k=3 case of Szemeredi's theorem.
